title: Tenancy mode setting: one synth-time switch, 'dedicated' (default) or 'shared'
description:
Outcome: Several shared-stack differences (no guest API reads, no subscriptions, no global group rules, no wildcard purge, tenant from the caller, no bundled site files, hooks refused) need one switch read at synth time and at run time. Add tenancy: { mode: "dedicated" | "shared" } to the site backend config (default dedicated, so every existing site is unchanged), pass it to functions as PAPYRUS_TENANCY_MODE, and expose one helper in Python (papyrus_content.tenancy) and TypeScript (lib/tenant-keys.ts) so code asks 'is this a shared stack?' in one way. Worktree Papyrus-worktrees/tenancy-mode (beside the Papyrus checkout), branch feature/<this id>-tenancy-mode.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): amplify/site-backend-config.ts, amplify/site-backend.ts (environment for functions), amplify/data/schema.ts (helper to vary rules by mode, unused yet), src/papyrus_content/tenancy.py, lib/tenant-keys.ts, docs/multi-tenancy.md.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenancy-mode.feature):
Scenario: An existing site synthesises exactly as before
    Given a site config with no tenancy setting
    When the backend is synthesised
    Then the template is identical to the previous release's

Scenario: Functions on a shared stack know it
    Given tenancy mode "shared"
    When content-actions starts
    Then the tenancy helper reports shared in Python and in TypeScript

Dependencies: blocked by nothing. Blocks PPY-baa75d, PPY-e01d82, PPY-daf673, PPY-ca247b. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: -.

Testing: npm run typecheck; npm test (add scripts/test-tenancy-mode.ts); poetry run pytest src/papyrus_content/tenancy_test.py; npm run test:schema-parity; synth snapshot comparison.
Rollout: Releasable alone; no behaviour change on any site.
Risk and mitigation: Low. Risk: a second, competing switch appears later. Mitigation: the helper is the only reader and a lint forbids reading the variable directly.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
